claim.pdf_says: D.2.2   File organization / D.2.2.1   Sequential organization  [printed page 1005] ... D.2.2.2   Relative organization  [printed page 1006]
claim.markdown_says: #### D.2.2 File organization / #### D.2.2.1 Sequential organization  (page-1035 slice) ... ## D.2.2.2 Relative organization  (page-1036 slice)
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown heading depth allegedly resets at every PDF page break instead of tracking the clause number, so D.2.2.2 is emitted at '##' - the same level as the '## Page 1036' scaffolding heading and two levels ABOVE its own parent D.2.2 ('####'). In any generated table of contents or heading-driven navigation, D.2.2.2 through D.2.2.5.3 detach from D.2.2 and read as peers of the annex itself. No normative text is lost (the clause number is preserved inline in the heading text), so this is structural, not normative. Claimed to be systemic: D.2.3.2.3 at '##' under D.2.3.2 at '###', D.2.4.3.1 at '##' vs sibling D.2.4.3.2 at '###', and a document-wide census of 2304 '##' / 1413 '###' / 96 '####'.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. No heading is missing and no PDF content is lost, altered, or added; the finding is a markdown-formatting observation misfiled as a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. (1) THE HEADING IS PRESENT, VERBATIM AND COMPLETE. Rendered spec_p1036.png (printed page 1006) carries exactly one clause heading: bold serif 'D.2.2.2 Relative organization'. The page-1036.md slice carries '## D.2.2.2 Relative organization' preceded by an explicit '' anchor. Clause number, title text, ordering and all three body paragraphs match glyph-for-glyph. The kind label 'missing-heading' is factually wrong - nothing is missing. (2) THE PDF ENCODES NO DEPTH FOR THE MARKDOWN TO LOSE. I looked at the printed glyphs on page 1005: 'D.1 General', 'D.2 Files', 'D.2.1 General', 'D.2.2 File organization' and 'D.2.2.1 Sequential organization' are ALL set in the identical bold serif at the identical point size, with identical left indent and identical spacing. Page 1006's 'D.2.2.2 Relative organization' is set the same way. ISO does not vary heading typography by clause depth in Annex D at all - depth is conveyed SOLELY by the dotted clause number, and the markdown preserves that number exactly. There is therefore no depth signal in the source document that the transcription failed to carry. A '#' count is metadata the markdown layer invents; it cannot 'disagree with' a PDF that has no such attribute. (3) THIS IS FORMATTING / PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE, AN EXPLICIT REJECT CRITERION. The level change coincides with the '---' + '' + '## Page 1036' scaffolding block - i.e. exactly the page-break furniture the transcription inserts and the PDF does not contain. Meaning is unchanged: 'D.2.2.2' is unambiguously a child of 'D.2.2' by its own number, and the stable anchor makes it addressable regardless of '#' count. (4) THE CLAIM'S CAUSAL STORY IS ITSELF WRONG, WHICH UNDERCUTS IT FURTHER. The depth is not a clause-depth mapping that 'resets at page breaks' - it is never a clause-depth mapping. On page 1005, with NO page break intervening, the markdown emits '#### D.2.2 File organization' and then '#### D.2.2.1 Sequential organization' at the SAME level, though D.2.2.1 is a child of D.2.2. The same non-mapping appears in normative body text far from any annex: '## 13.4 File section' ... '### 13.4.1' ... '### 13.4.4' then '## 13.4.5 File description entry' (a child of 13.4, emitted at its parent's level), then '### 13.4.5.2'. The transcription uses a shallow local heading rhythm document-wide; the page boundary is a coincidence, not the cause. (5) THE SUPPORTING CENSUS IS MISLEADING. I re-ran it: 2304 '##', 1413 '###', 96 '####' are correct raw counts, but 1261 of the 2304 '##' lines are '## Page NNNN' scaffolding, leaving only ~1043 actual '##' clause headings. The claim cites the inflated 2304 as evidence of a page-local reset; more than half of that number is the page furniture itself and says nothing about clause depth. The two sibling examples cited (D.2.3.2.3 at '##' under D.2.3.2 at '###'; D.2.4.3.1 at '##' vs D.2.4.3.2 at '###') do check out in the file, so the observation that markdown heading depth is inconsistent is TRUE - it is simply not a discrepancy against the PDF. If the project wants clause-number-driven heading depth for ToC generation, that is a transcription-tooling enhancement to raise on its own terms, not a spec-reconciliation defect, and it must not be logged in the reconciliation ledger as lost or altered spec content.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. Heading 'D.2.2.2 Relative organization' is transcribed completely and verbatim from printed page 1006, with its clause number intact and a '' anchor; all body text matches. The PDF sets every Annex D clause heading (D.1, D.2, D.2.1, D.2.2, D.2.2.1, D.2.2.2) in the same bold serif at the same size, so it encodes no heading depth for the transcription to lose - depth lives only in the dotted clause number, which is preserved. The observed markdown '#'-depth inconsistency is real but internal to the markdown and is not page-break-driven as claimed: D.2.2 and D.2.2.1 are both emitted at '####' on the same page with no break between them, and the same parent/child level collision occurs in normative body text (e.g. '## 13.4' / '## 13.4.5'). The claim's census is also inflated - 1261 of the 2304 '##' lines are '## Page NNNN' scaffolding. Route as an optional transcription-tooling improvement (derive heading level from the clause number), not as a spec-reconciliation finding.
